# gita-tyaga-sannyasa-zero-algebra-corroboration-study

**Scope(s):** `OBJECT` · **Row count:** 4 · **Lifecycle (candidate):** ACTIVE · **Layer (provisional):** LAYER-UNRESOLVED
**Notations:** `Mokṣa-Sannyāsa-Yoga ch.18`, `sannyāsa vs tyāga` · **Aliases:** `The Gītā on Elimination`
**Candidate group membership (NOT an identity claim):**
Ungrouped — no mechanical signal connected this label to any other in P2a.

## Sources (how this label entered the ledger)
- **OBJECT-INDEX** (batch B0063, scope OBJECT): A disciplined philosophical-interpretation study run alongside KR-ZERO-ALGEBRA-2026-09, restricted by Theory v1.2's ban on Gita-concept->primitive->architecture promotion to producing only questions/lenses/corroborations. Finds three genuine corroborations against the executed KR-ZERO-ALGEBRA results (all classified [EXT]/lens, never adopted): (C-1) Gita 18.2's distinction between renouncing an action (sannyasa) versus renouncing its fruit (tyaga) corroborates the experiment's finding that two of three candidate Remainder constructions coincide exactly (A=C, 1182/1182 cases) while the third (transformation residual) differs -- 'the residue of the operation is not the residue of the concern'; (C-2) 18.48's injunction not to abandon flawed-but-native work corroborates the 16.03% boundary-preservation finding (196/1,223 blocked eliminations); (C-3), called the strongest, is that the Gita's three-way classification of tyaga by its GROUND (tamasa/rajasa/sattvika) rather than its outcome corroborates the experiment's PATH-A-vs-PATH-B finding (55.75% agreement, markedly asymmetric: 1,559 over-removed vs 301 under-removed) -- 'an elimination is not adequately characterised by what it removes; it is characterised by the ground on which it removes it.' Explicitly finds NO textual support for the algebraic results (H5/H6 group-non-compositionality, non-confluence, termination, H9 invariant!=Zero) and refuses to name any kernel candidate, citing the experiment's own final-status rule and its own prior four-in-a-row record of yielding no kernel entities from Gita material.
